attempts.url: no OpenAPI 3.x; Azure publishes its data-plane APIs as Swagger 2.0 in Azure/azure-rest-api-specs

attempts.note: newest folder under stable/, but future-dated on 2026-11-16 (adds 4 operations); not captured until that api-version is current

notes: Full coverage of the Azure Blob Storage data-plane API (api-version 2026-10-06, the newest stable version in Azure/azure-rest-api-specs that is not future-dated as of 2026-11-16), converted from Microsoft's own Swagger 2.0 document committed verbatim as upstream.json — the conversion is 1:1 (69 operations and 56 definitions in, 69 operations and 56 component schemas out): service properties/stats, containers, leases, block/append/page blobs, blocks, pages, snapshots, copy, tiers, tags, immutability and legal hold. Replaces a 5 KiB hand-authored spec. Two Azure Swagger extensions are normalised on the way through: x-ms-paths (operations that differ only by query string, which plain OpenAPI paths cannot key) merge into paths with the ? rendered as a # fragment, and x-ms-parameterized-host becomes a templated server with a {url} variable, since the account name is part of the hostname. Blob is the only Azure Storage service the adaptor speaks (uploadBlob, downloadBlob, getBlobProperties — all present); Queue, Table and File are separate services with their own specs. Upstream moved on 2026-11-16: Azure renamed the spec folder from data-plane/Microsoft.BlobStorage to data-plane/BlobStorage (the old specUrl 404s; the 2021-12-02 file at the new path is byte-identical to the previous capture, sha256:c18611fc…), and the folder now carries stable versions up to 2027-03-07. The capture was moved from 2021-12-02 to 2026-10-06, the newest version dated on or before the capture day: same 69 operations and 56 definitions, content changes only. 2027-03-07 was not used because it is future-dated and a storage account may not accept it yet; it adds four operations (Blob_GetLayout, Container_CreateSession, and Apache Arrow variants of the flat and hierarchy blob listings) and five definitions, which the next refresh should pick up once that version is current. From 2025-11-05 on each version folder also holds a TypeSpec-generated generated_blob.json (the readme's default tag); the hand-maintained blob.json is kept as the source because it preserves the operationIds and path keys of the previous capture, whereas the generated file renames 15 operationIds and re-keys every path. File responses (autorest's {type: object, format: file}, e.g. Get Blob) are served as */* binary rather than under the document-wide application/xml, since a blob comes back in its own content type.
